info.title: solved.ac API
info.description:
Every request needs a client's `x-client-id` and `x-client-secret`.

Each operation's `x-access` says who may call it. `public` answers any app; it sees the user behind a user token only when the token holds the operation's `scope`, and otherwise answers as to no user. `user` acts for a user and needs a user token holding the named `scope`: without one `401` with code `USER_TOKEN_REQUIRED`, and with one lacking the scope `403` with `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

User tokens come from OAuth 2.0's authorization code grant with PKCE (S256 only). Send the user to `https://solved.ac/oauth/authorize` with `response_type=code`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` (exactly one registered in the console), `scope` (space-separated; `profile` is always included), `state`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`. Exchange the code at `POST /api/v4/oauth/token`, authenticating as the app, and send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer` beside the app's own credentials. A token works only for the app it was issued to. Users see the apps they granted, and disconnect them, in their settings.

Rate limits are token buckets. Each caller (a signed-in user, or an address) has a budget of 600 units per client, refilled at 2 per second, and a third-party client also has budgets its callers share: one the same size for requests without a user token, and one 200 times that for requests with one, which all the app's users share. All of them scale with the client's multiplier. A request costs 1 unit; problem search costs 3 and vote listings 2. Sign-in, sign-up, recovery and other actions a person takes have their own small limits. Past a budget, requests get `429` with `Retry-After`; responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.

Problem searches without a user, which today is every app's, are held to queries of 100 characters and 8 terms; past them they get `401` with code `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` and `details.limit` naming the limit. Leaderboards page freely for apps.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code, or a refresh token, for tokens
post.description:
The app authenticates as itself: `x-client-id` and `x-client-secret`, or HTTP Basic with the same pair. The body is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (or JSON) with:

- `grant_type=authorization_code`: `code`, `redirect_uri` (exactly the one the authorization request named) and `code_verifier` (PKCE, S256).
- `grant_type=refresh_token`: `refresh_token`, and optionally `scope` to narrow what the new tokens carry.

An access token lasts an hour. A refresh token comes only with `offline.access`, lasts 90 days, and is spent when used: each refresh returns a new one. A refresh token presented a second time ends that sign-in, every token of it, on the assumption that it was copied.
